stories.title: NLCS Game 4 Recap — Brewers 6, Dodgers 4; Milwaukee One Win From First World Series Since 1982
stories.angle: Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead solo homer off Tanner Scott in the sixth inning, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 to take a commanding 3-1 series lead. Milwaukee is one win away from its first World Series appearance since 1982 — 44 years. Game 5 is tonight at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers must win or their season ends. Glasnow was scheduled to start for LA.

stories.title: ALCS Game 3 Recap — Guardians 3, Rays 2; Halpin's Eighth-Inning Homer Gives Cleveland the Edge
stories.angle: Rookie outfielder Petey Halpin delivered a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning, and Cleveland beat Tampa Bay 3-2 to take a 2-1 series lead. The Rays — missing their ace Shane McClanahan — have now lost homefield advantage and face a must-win Game 4 TONIGHT at Progressive Field (8 PM ET, TBS). Two days after Freddy Peralta struck out Halpin to end an inning in Game 2, the rookie answered back.

stories.title: Ohtani's October — .150 Average, 0 Home Runs, and One Game Left to Write a Different Story
stories.angle: Shohei Ohtani hit .277 with 30 home runs in the regular season, but his postseason has been a nightmare. He's hitting .150 with zero home runs and seven strikeouts in the NLCS. He hasn't gone deep since August 18 in the regular season. The Dodgers' $700M investment faces elimination tonight in Game 5. A single postseason swing could change the conversation — but so far, October has been his worst month in a Dodgers uniform.

stories.title: Game 5 Preview — Glasnow and the Dodgers' Last Stand at Chavez Ravine

One bad inning from Glasnow could end the dynasty. How Milwaukee has limited LA's offense to four runs in two straight games is the story of this series.

stories.title: Petey Halpin — The Guardians' Rookie Who Silenced Tampa Bay's Ace
stories.angle: In Game 2, Freddy Peralta fired up after striking out Petey Halpin on a 3-2 changeup. In Game 3, Halpin crushed a two-run homer off the Rays' bullpen in the eighth to give Cleveland the lead for good. The rookie outfielder has become the surprise hero of the 2026 ALCS. He hit a three-run homer against the White Sox in September — now he's doing it in October, when it counts. Cleveland leads the ALCS 2-1 with Game 4 tonight.

x_posts.text:

The Guardians have found their October surprise. #Guardians #ALCS
